## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 55, titled *Bhiṁsāpana* ("Scaring a monk"), is a training rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka governing monastic conduct. The text sets out the disciplinary precept that a monk who intentionally frightens or scares another monk incurs an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*). An English translation of the rule and its exposition is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 It also shares curated parallels across multiple non-Theravāda Vinaya recensions preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan, including those of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya traditions.
